solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Against mum's the word "nonsense"

parts.note: to can mean against, as in setting a shoulder to the wheel
an instruction to keep quiet, which is the call for silence sh

explanation.surface: Someone urged to keep quiet is told to dismiss the talk as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum's the word' is a British saying meaning keep it secret; here it stands for the hushing sound SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British slang for rubbish talk, a synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Great many turned up about London, say, as the top attraction

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the city word
in a down entry the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lot is a great many
London is an example of a capital city

explanation.surface: Crowds turn out in London to see its star attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads the word for a great many backwards, and 'about' wraps it round the city; London is only an example of a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces the crowning point that tops everything else, the final extra on a list.

clue.text: Petty quarrel gets personal — cure may be found here

parts.note: a spat is a minor row
personal, as in your very own

explanation.surface: A minor row becomes personal and someone suggests a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort with mineral springs, such as Bath, where visitors went to take healing waters.

clue.text: £51 rise arranged? This might make things go smoothly

definitions.text: This might make things go smoothly

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals and a quid is British slang for one pound, so fifty-one pounds is LI quid

indicators.note: the letters of rise are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A pay rise of fifty-one pounds might be just the thing to smooth matters over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' scrambles RISE into ISER. A quid is British slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: A blender purees food until it is smooth, so it literally makes things go smoothly.

clue.text: Long sit-in arranged in left-leaning London borough

indicators.note: the letters of long sit-in are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A protest sit-in staged in a London district known for its left-wing politics.
explanation.definitionFit: This north London borough is famously linked with left-wing politicians and liberal residents.

clue.text: European Union up for supporting German and extreme

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting part goes beneath the German word

parts.note: und is German for and

indicators.note: in a down entry the letters are read upward

explanation.surface: A European body's support for Germany is seen as going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EU into UE; 'for supporting' puts it below UND.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive, beyond what is warranted, as with undue force, is a synonym of extreme.

clue.text: Classify as separate after definite mutating

indicators.note: mutating means changing form, so the letters change their order

explanation.surface: Something is labelled distinct once its definite form has changed.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell things apart and treat them as distinct is to distinguish between them.

clue.text: Reserved space putting in new court for the centre of Salisbury

indicators.note: the new letters are placed in the city's old name
they replace the middle letter of the old name

parts.note: Sarum is the old name of Salisbury, still used in Old Sarum

explanation.surface: A cathedral close set aside in the middle of Salisbury.
explanation.walkthrough: Salisbury, an English cathedral city, was once Sarum; swap its central R for NCT.
explanation.definitionFit: A private inner room where one is safe from intrusion is a space kept apart.

clue.text: List of those working for Catholic court

definitions.meaning: a duty schedule showing who is on which shift
the Roman ... is the Vatican's appeal tribunal

explanation.surface: A roster of staff on duty in a church tribunal.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a staff schedule; the other is the papal court of appeal.

clue.text: Opening large part of church

parts.note: an opening is an opportunity, a chance
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An opportunity arises to enter a big section of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The area around the altar reserved for clergy and choir is a named section of a church building.

clue.text: Bridging a gap to get over very popular river

parts.note: to cross is to get over to the other side
cult, as in a cult following
the Ural is a Russian river

explanation.surface: Someone builds a bridge over a gap to reach a fashionable river.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanning different societies or traditions is bridging the gap between them.

clue.text: Obsolete furnace regularly comes in handy

indicators.note: the selected letters enter the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: handy means skilful, deft

indicators.note: every other letter of furnace is taken, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: An old furnace that no longer works still proves useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of furnace, and 'comes in' puts them inside the word for handy, which here means skilful, not convenient.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer in use or existing is defunct, a synonym of obsolete.

clue.text: Perhaps I fix judgement

parts.note: the word I is an example of a part of speech standing in for a noun
to fix in place is to cement

explanation.surface: Someone may be the one to settle a ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' flags that I is an example of a pronoun, not the letter or the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal declaration or verdict delivered by an authority is a judgement.

clue.text: Like a gut feeling during exam over last missing header

indicators.note: in a down entry the earlier pieces sit over the trimmed word

parts.note: in can mean during, as in in the night
a test is an exam

indicators.note: the word loses its top letter

parts.note: final means last

explanation.surface: A hunch felt while sitting an exam about the last question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing header' drops F from FINAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the gut, the bowels, which a gut feeling is figuratively said to come from.

clue.text: What will hold little new in clothes

indicators.note: the short letter goes into the word for clothes

parts.note: togs is informal British for clothes
N is the short form of new

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about what will fit in some small new outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals the abbreviation N; 'in' puts it inside TOGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping implement with two arms is used to pick up and hold things such as coal or salad.

clue.text: Swimming rat is with an aquatic mammal dealer

indicators.note: swimming suggests letters thrashing about into a new order

parts.note: the desman is a small water-dwelling relative of the mole

explanation.surface: A rat swims alongside some other water creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' scrambles RAT into TRA. The desman is a little-known molelike animal of European and Russian rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper or merchant who buys and sells goods is a dealer.

clue.text: A mother pig that's found in mud?

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
swine are pigs

explanation.surface: A sow wallowing in the mud.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the pig is found in mud; the definition is water, which mud contains, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorous old phrase for water, the only drink in Eden, which mud is full of.

clue.text: Country's in the middle of Blitz — thus panic, man

indicators.note: each of the four words loses its first and last letters, leaving only its inner part

explanation.surface: A nation caught up in a bombing raid, its people panicking.
explanation.walkthrough: The insides of bLITz, tHUs, pANIc and mAn join up.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baltic state on the Baltic Sea, with Vilnius as its capital.

clue.text: Tail end of shift hours leading subordinate to crack?

indicators.note: only the final letter of shift is wanted

parts.note: under, as in someone under a manager

explanation.surface: At the end of a shift a junior is close to breaking down.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack of thunder is the loud sound after lightning; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Walrus, perhaps with the beginning of tusk pain

indicators.note: only the opening letter of tusk is wanted

parts.note: a dull pain is an ache

explanation.surface: A walrus suffering with a sore tusk.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal is a red herring: a walrus is also a style of drooping moustache, and 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tache is British slang for a moustache, and the bushy walrus is one kind.

clue.text: Loose garment with edging is used in church

indicators.note: the hem and the following word go into the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a hem is the edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A trimmed robe is worn in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' puts the edging word and 'is' inside the Church of England abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift dress or slip hanging straight from the shoulders is a loose garment.

clue.text: Obscure university name one with child identifying as the other sex

parts.note: trans describes a person whose gender identity differs from that assigned at birth
a mother or father, someone who has a child

explanation.surface: An obscure college lists one parent as having changed gender.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in a different order from the clue: the gender word sits before the parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not see-through or clear is obscure, as murky glass is.

clue.text: Expert working on involving deputy

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: at, as in hard at it

explanation.surface: A specialist gets busy with the help of an assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' wraps the two letters for 'working on', as in hard at it, round the short form of deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone highly skilled at something is an expert.

clue.text: British raised charge for grouse

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is read upward

parts.note: a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: Britain increases the fee for shooting game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The game bird is a red herring: grouse is a verb, to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is slang for complaining, the same as to grouse.

clue.text: Sanction sellers? Not very English

indicators.note: not here says the letter for very is to be left out of the sellers

parts.note: vendors are people who sell

explanation.surface: Should traders be approved? Not especially English ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' drops the very letter V from the sellers; the question mark hides that the first sentence is wordplay, not a question.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve or give official support to something is to sanction it.

clue.text: Old language of a Roman emperor, missing core of Latin

indicators.note: the central letter of Latin is lost from the adjective

parts.note: Tiberian means relating to the emperor Tiberius

indicators.note: the core of a five-letter word is its third letter

explanation.surface: A dead tongue linked to an emperor, without the heart of Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core of' picks T from laTin; 'missing' drops it from TIBERIAN. The surface suggests Latin itself is the old language.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient tongue spoken in the Spanish peninsula before Roman conquest is an extinct language.

clue.text: Message to many that might have felt tremor in a quake

indicators.note: a quake shakes the letters of felt tremor into a different order

explanation.surface: A mass mailing that might have reported a tremor felt during an earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard letter sent unchanged to many recipients is a circular message.

clue.text: Knock down chap that emits a cry of pain

indicators.note: emitting sends something out, so the cry leaves the word for chap

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
ow is what someone says when hurt

explanation.surface: A man who has been knocked over yelps in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that emits' takes OW out of FELLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell a tree or a boxer is to bring it down to the ground.
